intro.summary: Create a window, clear its back buffer with Direct3D 11, and present your first frame.
overview.heading: When to use Direct3D 11
overview.purpose: Direct3D 11 is Microsoft's graphics API for Windows. It works well for 3D games, editors, and visualizations. The runtime tracks resource states and handles much of the synchronization.
overview.choice: Choose Direct3D 11 for a Windows project if you want a simpler way into DirectX than Direct3D 12, or if you already have a Direct3D 11 renderer. For a similarly approachable cross-platform option, consider OpenGL.
requirements.heading: 1. Set up the project
requirements.folder: In the LIMEN source directory, create a folder named first-d3d11. Save the next section's code as Main.hx inside it.
requirements.paragraph: Follow the LIMEN installation guide and copy limen.hdll and d3d11.limen into the app directory. You need Windows and a GPU that supports Direct3D 11. Use source files and native modules from the same LIMEN version.
program.heading: 2. Render your first frame
program.intro: Get the back buffer, create a render target view, and clear it. After presenting the frame, the event loop keeps the window open.
run.heading: 3. Build, run, and experiment
run.runtime: Run the commands from the directory containing Main.hx. If you use the bundled Windows runtime, copy hl.exe and libhl.dll from the build output into that directory and run .\hl.exe main.hl.
run.result: A window with a blue background should open. Close it, change the color or title in Main.hx, and run both commands again.
